newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Europe to examine Boeing/McDonnell merger.
newsitem.headline: Europe to examine Boeing/McDonnell merger.

text.p: The European Commission will examine the planned merger between Boeing Co. and McDonnell Douglas Corp., European Union Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said Wednesday.

Van Miert said the EU executive body had had contacts with the two companies and expected to receive a formal notification of the deal within weeks. "I can confirm that the commission is going to examine the matter," he said.
Earlier on Wednesday he told a European Parliament committee that there had been contacts with the parties concerned. "This is a case with which the Commission has to deal," he said.
Van Miert repeated the commission's position that granting European Union clearance to the merger under competition rules could be difficult.

"This is a difficult case. Boeing has 60 percent of the commercial airline (market). While McDonnell's market share is going down, it still adds to Boeing's," he told the parliament, adding that the commission would need to look at deal's effects.
In December, Van Miert warned both companies that their planned $13.3 billion merger could hurt competition in Europe.
He has said the commission would have to examine the deal closely to assess whether it would strengthen the hold of the merged companies over any product or market in the European Union.
On Wednesday, he said this could be a long process.
"This will take some time. It is complicated," he said, adding there would be a "thorough and vigorous" examination.

Under EU rules, the commission has one month to complete a routine investigation if a merger falls within the scope of the bloc's merger regulation. If it needs more time for a detailed analysis, it can start a four-month second stage probe.
